Schools don't do a good job when teaching anything to do with computing. While I'm a Linux fan I don't think it is appropriate for a school that just wants to teach kids the basics of using a computer to get work done. If they were programming, then yes, Linux. Windows and OSX shouldn't either be used because they cost more, are higher maintenance and if you're teaching the concepts then Linux is just as good. If you're not teaching computing, then chromebooks are perfect. I was taught computing at school and I do very well these days but I look at kids who were taught on PCs after I left and they can barely function because they didn't learn the concepts, just what button to click. My point was for basic tasks. Taking notes, researching things, writing papers. I think familiarizing students with what they should be using would be better. I am fairly firmly in the camp that open source should be the norm and in that case there isn't anything better than Linux. My issue with Chromebooks being that too much of what they do happens in a way that is uncontrolled by the user. For school or work, that's not much of an issue. However, what people use in school tends to be what the use at home.

Well, much of the reason why Windows is such a zoo with all that malware is because it is in the hands of so many people who don't really need a full computer and rather they need something that is more of a device like a phone or tablet, but something with a bigger screen and a keyboard. At this time, I think chromebooks are the best option for that. Most people don't need to know how the computer works and don't need to be looking after it. Again, I'm a programmer who uses all platforms and looks after his own system, plus I'm a Linux admin on a large environment so I'm used to this stuff but most of my users and the people I know personally too aren't really interested. Schools aren't teaching computing, they're teaching kids how to function. The skills they learn on a Chromebook are going to work just as well on any other computer. The good part for the school is they don't need to worry about all the fiddling with keeping a proper computer safe so it is better for the school, cheaper, and also the kids get what they need without all that operating system fluff going on.

If the kids are learning computing, and have a teacher who can teach it (that's the key because so much of the reason why kids can't use computers is down to the teacher's own inability and you end up with lowest common denominator teaching, and just teaching the actions without the why) then Linux labs are undoubtably the way to go. Windows and OS X shouldn't be in schools at all. There's nothing they can offer that can't be done on Linux and that's also coming from sone who's primary machine is a MacBook.
